title: HPR Community News July 2024
blurb: HPR volunteers review shows released and comments posted in July 2024, discuss new hosts, website improvements, and future community engagement.

summary.purpose: The meeting served to review shows released and comments posted on Hacker Public Radio during July 2024 and discuss community-related topics.

keyTakeaways.point: Two new hosts, Trolla Costa and The Lucky Boy, joined HPR in July.
A significant discussion on the future of HPR, community engagement, and the effectiveness of current communication channels was prompted by Nightwise's show.
A project is underway to repair 352 HPR shows that lost external files during a website migration, with 148 already completed.
Volunteers are needed to staff an HPR booth at the Spectrum 24 conference in Paris to promote the network and attract new hosts.
The legalities and ethics of archiving public works, particularly regarding copyright and permission, were debated.

topics.heading: Introduction of New Hosts
points: Trolla Costa and The Lucky Boy joined HPR.
They contributed two very good shows.

topics.heading: July Show Reviews and Comments
points: Urandom Pirate Episodes: A fun show about mending things with a neighbor guest.
Comments on previous shows: Discussion on wood finishing, teleprinters, and 'Studio C' setups.
'About' page update: Foundation for future HPR changes, aiming to consolidate repeated content.
GNU Sleep Tips: Overview of the 'sleep' command, noting GNU enhancements like minutes/hours and notification messages.
Badger 2040: A programmable e-ink display badge from Pimoroni, programmable in Python.
Krita Interview: An excellent interview with the author of Krita, highlighting its use for artistic work and comic strips.
Alexander's Introduction: A brilliant first show, confidently delivered despite initial nervousness.
New Year's Eve Show: An eclectic 3-hour show covering diverse topics from autism to Levi Jeans, with excellent show notes.
Passkeys: An enlightening show on passkeys and their security impact, prompting awareness of related issues.
Retro Game Console: Kevin's experience building a retro game console with Raspberry Pi for £151.
HPR Music Project: 'The Walking Tune' by Appleball, a traditional folk tune with Scottish/Irish similarities.
Samba and Tiny Computers: Al's show on using a Lenovo ThinkCentre M700 Tiny for Samba and other tasks, prompting interest in Proxmox.
Postgraduate Computing: Lee's challenging experience with an MSc in Computer Science at the Open University.
A Circle of Moss: An interview with Moss Bliss, discussing his performing experience and diverse facets.
Software Freedom Day: A call to action for organizing meetups, noting the decline post-COVID.
Removing Obstacles: BISA's show on using text-to-speech for HPR shows, addressing discomfort with public speaking.
Beyond Economic Recovery: Discussion on archiving, legal ownership, and the right to control access to public works.
Playing Civilization: Part 3 Part 5, the final episode in a strategy game series.
Bathroom Renovation: Al's brave project renovating his bathroom, including plumbing and shower installation.
Up-directed for Piper XQs: Archer 72 demonstrating 'up-directed' on Fedora, potentially integrating into HPR workflow.
Adding Storage to MacBook Pro: Siftle on 10's experience with SSDs, highlighting their failure rates and data loss.

topics.heading: Future of HPR and Community Engagement
points: Discussion prompted by Nightwise's show on HPR's future.
Nightwise's critical feedback on outdated comment systems, mailing lists, and lack of listener-to-host conversion.
Concerns about hosts burning out due to lack of feedback and 'screaming into the void'.
Nightwise's decision to step down as a host due to burnout and feeling unheard.
Brian Neverett's feedback on the simplicity of the comment system via AntennaPod but difficulty with CAPTCHA.

topics.heading: HPR Show Repair Project
points: Dave Norris is repairing HPR shows with lost external files (pictures, videos, scripts) from a previous migration.
The process involves copying files from the Internet Archive and backup disks and re-linking them.
Out of 352 shows needing repair, 148 have been completed, with 214 remaining.

nextSteps: HPR will hold its next Community News meeting in September.
Listeners are encouraged to listen to and comment on Nightwise's show about the future of HPR.
Dave Norris will give a talk about amateur radio on the HPR network at the Spectrum 24 conference.
The project to repair HPR shows with lost external files will continue.

actionItems.text: Consolidate 'about' page content as part of the website redesign to avoid repetition.
Do a show on Proxmox, ideally covering its licensing aspects and reasons for use.
Make a follow-up show on web mining to delve deeper into how the stuff was built.
Get in touch with Jim Devoy to help out with the podcast dog catcher project.
Document the show repair process in the AOB section.
